newsitem.title: INDIA: India copper bounces back as zinc climbs.
newsitem.headline: India copper bounces back as zinc climbs.

text.p: Copper prices bounced back while zinc climbed up on the local market on Tuesday, dealers said.
Other base metals remained steady in a narrow price band.

Copper prices moved up by 50 rupees at 13,650 rupees per quintal on the back of a rally in the world market which triggered fresh buying support. Copper was down by 50 rupees on Monday after losing 225 rupees last week.
Zinc prices rose by 50 rupees at 8,150 rupees as the upsurge in the world market triggered speculative interest.
"Zinc prices in the world market have gone up to their highest level in six years," one broker said.
Tin was steady at 29,000 rupees per quintal, as was nickel at 33,800 rupees per quintal. Last week tin was down 600 rupees and nickel by 500 rupees per quintal.
Aluminium stayed at the previous level of 7,700 rupees, as was lead at 4,100 rupees per quintal in nominal trade.
Overall volume remained slow during the day as major players kept to the sidelines, waiting for state-owned agencies to announce sale prices for the second half.
